sentences.text: The land of the petitioner was acquired under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
An award was made on 05.07.2018.
Aggrieved, the petitioner sought reference of the dispute to the Arbitrator in terms of Section 3G(5) of the Act.
The Arbitrator gave his award on 16.03.2021.

The petitioner has challenged the award of the Competent Authority dated 05.07.2018 and that of the Arbitrator dated 16.03.2021.
4.
The case of the petitioner is that his land was valued much more than what was determined by the Special Land Acquisition Officer and the Arbitrator.

It is also alleged that the land is adjacent to National Highway No. 7 as is evident from report of Tehsildar Chunar, District Mirzapur dated 12.03.2019 and therefore the valuation made is not in accordance with principles laid down under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
5.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: By Section 3G(6), the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 have been made applicable to every Arbitration under the National Highways Act, 1956.
Therefore, the petitioner had the remedy of challenging the award of the Arbitrator by filing objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, which he did not avail.
6. Therefore, no good ground is made out to entertain the challenge in exercise of writ jurisdiction.
7. The petition is dismissed with liberty to the petitioner to avail such other remedy as may be advised.
(Donadi Ramesh, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 13.9.2023
Ruhi H.
